newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian ex-diplomat in court on child sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Australian ex-diplomat in court on child sex charges.

text.p: A former senior Australian diplomat paid US$2.00 for sex with a teenage Cambodian boy he picked up in the gardens of a temple in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh, an Australian court heard on Monday.
The boy, 14, who cannot be named for legal reasons, told a magistrates court in Canberra that he had sex twice with former Australian ambassador to Cambodia John Holloway, 53.

Holloway is facing a committal hearing to decide if he should stand trial under a 1994 Australian law that provides for Australians to be prosecuted for sexual offences against children committed outside the country.
Holloway has not yet entered a plea. But his lawyer, Richard Refshauge, has previously said outside court that Holloway strongly denies the charge.
The Cambodian teenager's evidence, through an interpreter, was given by closed circuit television from a room outside the courtroom.
The boy told the hearing that a man who was Holloway's driver or interpreter picked him up at the temple's gardens in 1994 and drove him and Holloway to the former diplomats' house.
He said Holloway then performed oral sex on him. The boy said that on a later occasion, Holloway asked him to perform anal sex.
Holloway served as a senior adviser to the Cambodian government after his term as ambassador ended in 1994, but it is unclear which position he held at the time relating to the charges.

Holloway is the second Australian to be charged under the law, which carries a maximum penalty of 17 years jail. In April, a Sydney man was jailed for two years for an offence against a girl in the Philippines.
